title: Imaging Photoexcited Carrier Dynamics in Strontium Titanate Photocatalysts using Photomodulated Electron Energy-Loss Spectroscopy
content: Water-splitting nanoparticle bed reactors offer a promising pathway to renewably generate hydrogen. However, SrTiO3 nanoparticles have not yet reached external quantum efficiencies needed for commercial viability – even optimized catalysts produce an order of magnitude less hydrogen than predicted by thermodynamic efficiency estimates [1,2]. In this work, we study 2 at% Rh, La-codoped SrTiO3 nanoparticles using scanning TEM electron energy-loss spectroscopy (STEM-EELS) with photomodulation to relate the nanoparticle’s photoexcited electron and hole dynamics to their photoactivity. With this new photomodulated STEM-EELS approach, we differentiate the effects of photoexcited holes and heat at the nanometer scale by utilizing the low-loss spectrum’s sensitivity to valence band electrons.
